name: Chicken Meatballs in Cranberry Sauce

ingredients.buy: 5 cups (three and a half 14 oz cans)

writer_notes: All 17 locked ingredient lines are used by a step and no step uses anything unbought; verified both directions before submit.
No cost_lines were provided in the dispatch, so shop_smart makes only package-count claims sourced from the buy strings and no per-ounce or per-batch cost comparisons.
Cost, calories, and protein are written as tokens (${{cost_ps}}, {{cal}}, {{protein}}) per the templating rule; the only literal figures used are the buy-string package counts.
Protein locked to boneless skinless chicken breast per run condition; source turkey alternative and gluten-free flour option deliberately omitted from prose.

Flagged in detail: Worcestershire scales to 1/2 cup vs an expected ~7 tbsp, black pepper 3/4 tsp vs ~0.875 tsp, and the high 68.7 g carb load driven by cranberry sauce plus honey. Not fixed, flagged for the repair pass.

prose.intro_html:
Here is a dinner that tastes like a holiday and costs like a plain Tuesday. Ground chicken breast gets seasoned, rolled, browned in a pan, and then folded into a sweet cranberry sauce with just enough chili heat to keep it interesting. It is the kind of plate that makes people think you fussed, when really you ran a food processor and a skillet.

At {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per container, this is a real meal doing a real job. Cranberry and honey carry the sweetness, panko and whole wheat flour keep the meatballs tender, and the chicken does the heavy lifting on protein. You get comfort food that still answers to the numbers.
prose.shop_smart:
• Canned cranberry sauce comes in 14 oz cans. This batch calls for three and a half cans, so put four in the cart and let the leftover half hang around for morning toast or a sandwich.
  • The chicken is the engine here at 7 pounds of boneless skinless breast. Buy the biggest family pack the store puts on sale and skip anything labeled pre-ground, because you are grinding it yourself in the food processor for a fraction of the price.
  • Panko and whole wheat flour are small players, under a cup each. These are pantry staples you likely already own, so check the shelf before you buy a fresh bag.
  • Honey runs about seven eighths of a cup. A standard squeeze bottle covers it with room to spare.
  • Garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, chili powder, cayenne, and red pepper flakes are all dry pantry spices. Reach for the store brand jars; the name on the label does nothing your tongue can taste.
  • Worcestershire sauce and one bunch of fresh rosemary round it out. The rosemary is just a garnish, so a single sprig-bunch is plenty.
prose.make_it:
1. Drop the cubed chicken breast into a food processor and pulse until it is chopped. Add the panko, beaten egg, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, kosher salt, and black pepper, then pulse again until the meat is medium-fine and everything is folded through.
  2. With wet hands so nothing sticks, roll the mixture into balls about an inch across. Give each one a gentle roll in the whole wheat flour and shake off the extra.
  3. Heat a large non-stick pan over medium and drizzle in the olive oil. Working in batches so the pan is not crowded, add the meatballs and cook about 2 minutes per side, until they are golden brown and cooked through. Move each finished batch to a plate.
  4. Meanwhile, in a bowl, stir the cranberry sauce together with the honey, chili powder, cayenne, red pepper flakes, and a little salt and pepper until it is smooth and well combined.
  5. Pour the cranberry sauce over the meatballs, stir to coat, then drop the heat to low and simmer until it is bubbly, about 5 minutes. Scatter the fresh rosemary over the top and you are done.
prose.portion_html:
Fourteen even containers, no guessing. Set an empty container on the scale and note its weight. Then weigh the whole pan of meatballs and sauce, subtract the pan, and divide what is left by fourteen. That number is your target per container.

Scoop, weigh, and nudge until each one hits the mark, sauce and all. Every container lands at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein. Spoon it over rice or a pile of roasted vegetables at reheat time if you want to stretch the plate further.
prose.cost_closing_html:
At ${{cost_ps}} a serving, this is fourteen dinners that taste like a special occasion for less than what one takeout entree costs. The chicken you ground yourself is where the savings live, and the cranberry sauce does the fancy work for pennies.

Run the math on your week. Fourteen containers out of one afternoon means you are not deciding what to eat when you are tired and expensive decisions get made. The freezer takes the ones you will not reach in four days, and future you says thank you.

If this is the kind of cooking you want more of, the whole catalog runs the same way: real numbers, real grocery prices, no mystery. Membership is a dollar a month, which is roughly the change under your car seat, and it opens every recipe and every cost breakdown we have.

Cook once, eat all week, and let the plan do the worrying. That is the entire idea.

steps: In a food processor, pulse the cubed chicken breast until chopped. Add the panko, beaten egg, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, kosher salt, and black pepper, then pulse until the meat is medium-fine.
With wet hands, form the mixture into 1-inch balls. Roll each gently in the whole wheat flour and shake off the excess.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium and drizzle in the olive oil. Working in batches, add the meatballs and cook about 2 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
In a bowl, stir the cranberry sauce together with the honey, chili powder, cayenne, red pepper flakes, and a little salt and pepper until well combined.

Pour the cranberry sauce over the meatballs and stir to coat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer until bubbly, about 5 minutes, then garnish with fresh rosemary. Portion across 14 containers using the weigh method.
